meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Korea (Republic of Korea, unitary national jurisdiction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified commercial law under the Korean Commercial Act)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 17115, as amended), Articles 5-2, 8-2 and 9; Enforcement Decree provisions on customer due diligence and beneficial owner identification; Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 11245, as amended), Articles 22, 23, 289, 292 and 295; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Article 6; KoFIU examination and reporting guidelines; FATF Recommendation 24 as implemented by Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. Korea does not currently maintain a fully public UBO register; beneficial ownership data is collected by financial institutions and reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit for government access, supervisory inspection and law enforcement use.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or corporate registry of the jurisdiction of each ultimate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: (1) issue certified true copy from company registrar; (2) obtain Apostille from the competent authority of that state; (3) produce a certified Korean sworn translation. Non-member state: (1) issue certified true copy; (2) authenticate by the issuing country foreign ministry; (3) obtain Consular Legalization from the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that country; (4) produce a certified Korean sworn translation. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or equivalent corporate registry authority in the jurisdiction of the ultimate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: (1) obtain official Certificate of Good Standing; (2) affix Apostille by the competent local authority; (3) Korean sworn translation. Non-member state: (1) obtain official Certificate of Good Standing; (2) authenticate at the issuing country foreign ministry; (3) obtain Consular Legalization from the Korean consular post; (4) Korean sworn translation. Select only the route applicable to the issuing country; do not combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the ultimate parent or controlling shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: (1) execute or notarize the board resolution and power of attorney; (2) obtain Apostille on the notarial certificate or corporate document; (3) Korean sworn translation. Non-member state: (1) notarize the resolution and power of attorney; (2) authenticate by the issuing country competent ministry; (3) obtain Consular Legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate; (4) Korean sworn translation. The selected route depends solely on the Hague Convention membership of the issuing jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Ultimate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate shareholder or parent company, accompanied by a notarial certificate of current effect
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille state: (1) notarize the certified Articles of Association; (2) Apostille by the recognized competent authority; (3) Korean sworn translation. For a non-member state: (1) notarize the certified Articles of Association; (2) authenticate through the issuing country foreign ministry; (3) Consular Legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate; (4) Korean sworn translation. These routes are parallel alternatives under Korean due diligence practice.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Ultimate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution maintaining the operating or treasury account of the ultimate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention state: (1) bank officer signs the reference letter on letterhead; (2) notarization of the officer signature; (3) Apostille by the competent authority; (4) Korean sworn translation. Non-member state: (1) bank officer signs letter; (2) notarization; (3) authentication by issuing country foreign ministry; (4) Consular Legalization by the Korean consular post; (5) Korean sworn translation. The bank letter must identify account opening date, relationship tenor, transaction activity and any ML/CFT risk notices; choose one authentication route and never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sectoral sanctions lists, EU and UK HM Treasury consolidated lists, and Korean autonomous sanctions and export-control lists must be performed for all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, signatories, commercial counterparties, vessels, banks and insurance providers. Screening must use fuzzy matching on aliases, date of birth, passport numbers, maritime IMO numbers and historical name changes, and must be repeated in near-real time upon any sanctions list update, before each payment event, and at each change of corporate control. For all PEPs, including Korean domestic PEPs and foreign PEPs, undertake enhanced due diligence requiring independent verification of source of wealth and source of funds, senior management approval, ongoing transaction monitoring and a written risk assessment retained for at least five years after the relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office Internet Registration Service (i-RO) business name and trade name search module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registered name of a Korean Chusik Hoesa must be in the Korean script, Hangul; a Latin-script trade name may be used in translations and marketing but is not the registered statutory name. Transliteration must follow the Revised Romanization of Korean. The standard corporate naming format follows a four-tier convention: distinctive brand identifier, business purpose or industry descriptor, corporate form indicator Chusik Hoesa, and optional English trade name. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name in the same registry, and must be sufficient to distinguish the company from existing marks in the petroleum wholesale and marine fuel brokerage sector.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the registry officer, the applicant must obtain a written refusal stating the conflicting trade name. A request for review may be filed with the district court having jurisdiction over the registration office within two weeks, accompanied by evidence of prior use, trademark registrations, or consents from the holder of the conflicting name. If the court confirms the rejection, an immediate appeal is available to the appellate court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act. Foreign applicants should engage a licensed Korean administrative attorney and may seek a provisional disposition to compel the registry to conditionally reserve the cleared name while judicial review proceeds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the primary registered office for a Chusik Hoesa engaged in physical wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and distillates. The National Tax Service, relevant municipal licensing authority, and banks performing customer due diligence for high-risk energy commodity traders generally reject PO Box-only addresses and shared virtual business centres. The Petroleum Business Act and commercial registration practice require a physical location where legal notices can be served, corporate books are kept, original transaction records are available, and a responsible manager can attend regulatory inspections. A serviced physical office may be accepted only if the company maintains private suite signage, staffing, communication infrastructure, and segregated records at that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High, estimated at 75-85% probability within the first twelve months of licensing. The National Tax Service, local municipal government, and Korea National Oil Corporation inspection authorities conduct unannounced on-site inspections for petroleum wholesale and marine fuel brokers. Pre-inspection checklist includes: physical signage, active staffing, original business license and petroleum broker certificate, statutory transaction ledgers, customer contracts, vessel and storage terminal agreements, bank records, source of funds documentation, AML/CFT manual, compliance officer designation, data and telephone infrastructure, and evidence that management can produce records on demand. Failure to maintain substantive presence at the registered office may result in license revocation, tax registration cancellation, and bank account closure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee is levied for initial business registration in Korea.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Korean sworn translation of UBO, Board Resolution, Bank Reference Letter and corporate documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official government certificate fees and notarial fee schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for enhanced due diligence in high-risk petroleum commodity trading.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act, Act No. 1000, promulgated 1957, as last amended, Articles 167, 289, 290, 292, 295, 305, 317, 318 and 635; Korean Civil Act Articles 31 to 42; Enforcement Decree of the Korean Commercial Act; Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for non-resident shareholding and inward remittance reporting.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the principal place of business, such as the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office, administered under the Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation under Article 317 of the Korean Commercial Act, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the minutes of the incorporation meeting, and the first board resolution approving capitalization, banking, office, and officers.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required for a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act after the 2012 abolition of the minimum capital floor. However, each subscribed share must be fully paid before incorporation registration. The subscription money must be deposited into a bank account opened in the name of the corporation in the Republic of Korea, not a personal account of an incorporator. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a non-resident subscriber must file a foreign investment report with a designated foreign exchange bank or KOTRA and may be required to hold the inward remittance in a dedicated foreign investment escrow-type account to obtain a foreign investment certificate; such certificate is useful for later tax exemptions and license applications.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: ADOPTED by the unanimous written consent of the Board of Directors of ONDREAM KOREA CO., LTD. (the 'Corporation'), a Chusik Hoesa organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, on [●] day of [●], 2025. WHEREAS, the Corporation has been established to conduct the physical wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil, crude oil, refined petroleum products, and distillates, including international energy commodity trading and related payment services within the scope of ISIC 4661; and WHEREAS, the Korean Commercial Act and the notarized Articles of Incorporation authorize the Board to approve all matters necessary for the completion of statutory incorporation and initial corporate governance. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows. 1. Share Capital Subscription and Issuance. The Board ratifies the initial authorized share capital of [●] Korean won, divided into [●] ordinary shares with a par value of [●] Korean won each. The Board confirms that all subscriptions set out in the Subscription Register have been validly made and accepted, that the subscription price due on each subscribed share has been fully paid in cash to the Corporation’s designated bank account, and that the issued shares are fully paid, validly issued, and non-assessable. 2. Banking Authorization. The Board designates [●] Bank as the principal transaction bank of the Corporation. The Chief Executive Officer, jointly with the Chief Financial Officer, is expressly authorized to open and maintain corporate accounts, execute SWIFT wire transfers, establish standby letters of credit, negotiate maritime fuel purchase and sale settlements, and issue all payment instructions necessary for the energy wholesale business. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board adopts the office located at [●], Seoul, Republic of Korea, as the Corporation’s registered office. The legal representative is authorized to execute and deliver the lease or title documents, submit the registration of the head office address to the competent District Court Registry, and file the same address with the National Tax Service for business registration. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board appoints [●] as Chief Executive Officer, [●] as Chief Financial Officer, [●] as an inside director, and [●] as Statutory Auditor, each to hold office according to the Articles of Incorporation and the Korean Commercial Act. Each officer is authorized to execute contracts, sign share certificates, and represent the Corporation before courts, tax authorities, financial institutions, and licensing agencies. 5. Ratification and Implementation. The Board ratifies all lawful acts executed by the incorporators and officers in furtherance of the Corporation’s incorporation, licensing, and operational readiness. The officers are directed to complete all filings and satisfy all conditions precedent within the periods required by law. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the corporate minute book. Approved and executed on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search, Trademark Clearance, and Pre-Incorporation Governance Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office for company name search and the Korean Intellectual Property Office KIPRIS for trademark search.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Supreme Court of Korea online registry portal and perform an exact and homonym search of the proposed Korean and romanized corporate name to ensure that no identical company is already registered in any Korean jurisdiction. Conduct a KIPRIS search for identical or confusingly similar trademarks in international classes relevant to petroleum, fuel oil, energy, and trading services. Issue and retain a written clearance memorandum summarizing the name availability result, trademark status, and governance plan for the foreign beneficial owners. This due diligence protects the registration filing because the District Court Registry will suspend or reject an incorporation application if the proposed name is identical to an existing Korean company or is misleadingly similar in the same business scope.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Identification and passport copies of the proposed shareholders and directors
Power of attorney for any local formation agent
Trademark search output from KIPRIS
Corporate name search result from the Supreme Court registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court or registry queries the name, submit a corrective application with a revised name and a new trademark search report. If an objecting company raises prior use, provide evidence of distinctiveness or amend the name and restart the search; the curative window is 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and Adoption of the Initial Share Subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A notary public commissioned by the Seoul District Notaries Association under the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation containing all mandatory clauses required by Article 289 of the Korean Commercial Act, including corporate object, corporate name, total authorized shares, par value and class of shares, location of the registered head office, initial directors, statutory auditor, and the method of public notice if any. Each incorporator shall sign or affix a seal upon the document, and the session of incorporators shall approve the initial share subscription schedule and the list of subscribers. The notary public will examine nationality, legal capacity, legality of the object, and payment records, and shall then issue a notarial certificate entitling the formation to make a registration filing. In the same session, the incorporators adopt the resolutions in the minutes required for the subsequent first board of directors meeting.
required_dossiers: Executed draft of the Articles of Incorporation
Original identification documents of all incorporators and directors
Written allocation schedule of subscribed shares
Subscription registers signed by each subscriber
Power of attorney and incorporation instructions from foreign shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies Korean-language inconsistencies or unauthorized corporate objects, correct the articles, re-execute signatures, and present a revised version for re-notarization. A supplemental notarial addendum may cure minor defects without restarting the entire incorporation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Remittance and Deposit of Paid-In Share Capital and Foreign Investment Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A designated bank authorized under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, including KEB Hana Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank, or the foreign exchange desk of a commercial bank; KOTRA Invest Korea for foreign direct investment notification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate subscription account in the name of the Chusik Hoesa before registration. Each subscriber shall remit the full subscription price for every subscribed share into this account from a domestic or foreign account. Obtain an official deposit certificate from the bank stating the account holder, deposit date, aggregate amount in Korean won, and the purpose of deposit. For non-resident investors, file the foreign investment report with the designated bank or through KOTRA Invest Korea and obtain a foreign investment certificate. This certificate should match the total paid-in capital and the shareholding ratio to prevent future licensing and tax penalties. The deposit certificate is a mandatory attachment to the court registration application and must be preserved in original form.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Passports and alien registration visas of foreign investors
Remittance receipts or FX payment confirmation
Foreign investment notification form
AML and source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank withholds remittance because of anti-money-laundering review, submit notarized commercial contracts, bank statements, and beneficial ownership declarations. If the foreign investment report is rejected, correct the notification and refile with KOTRA or the delegated bank within 7 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Completion of Corporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered head office, for example the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office; filing may be made physically or through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statutory Application for Registration of Incorporation and assemble the full set of supporting documents, including the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the incorporators’ meeting minutes, the first board resolution, the paid-in capital deposit certificate, written consents of the appointed directors and statutory auditor, and the registered seal. Submit the application to the court registry and pay the court revenue stamp fee plus registration tax calculated at 0.4% of paid-in capital, with the 20% education surtax, unless reduced under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The registry will review the legal existence of the entity, the authenticity of signatures, and the validity of the corporate object. Upon approval, the court issues a certified certificate of registered items, which marks the legal existence of the corporation and permits the opening of permanent business bank accounts and the issuance of contracts.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank deposit certificate of paid-in capital
Minutes of the incorporation meeting and first board resolution
Letter of acceptance from each director and auditor
Corporate seal and seal certificate
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a suspension or correction notice, the applicant must cure the stated defects within 5 to 10 business days by filing supplemental documents. If the application is rejected, refile with a complete set of corrected documents and obtain a new receipt number; no additional notarization is required for ministerial corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Local Governing Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service through the HomeTax online portal and the local Si/Gun/Gu tax office for local registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after the court registration, file the application for a Business Registration Certificate using the corporate registration certificate, the lease agreement for the registered office, the articles of incorporation, the identification of the legal representative, and the corporate seal certificate. The tax authority assigns a business registration number used for value-added tax, corporate income tax, and electronic tax invoices. Simultaneously, register the corporate seal card and open a permanent corporate operating bank account. The business registration certificate must show the corporate name, address, business object, and representative in exactly the same wording as the court registration to avoid customs, petroleum licensing, and banking rejections.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration certificate from the court registry
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Lease or ownership document of the registered office
Corporate seal and seal certificate
Representative identification
Completed business registration application Form 10
Foreign investment certificate if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service delays because the address differs from the court registration, reconcile the address through a court amendment and resubmit the business registration application with the updated registration certificate and a new lease. The tax office appeal and correction process generally completes within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Licenses and Energy Sector Pre-Operation Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, Petroleum and Gas Division; the local Si/Gun/Gu government; the Korea Petroleum Supply Association; the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries for marine fuel service; and the Ministry of Environment for environmental approvals.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration and tax registration are complete, file the Petroleum Wholesale Business Registration application with the competent local government under the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act before executing any wholesale or brokerage transaction involving crude oil, marine fuel oil, or refined distillates. If the company owns or leases tank storage with a capacity above the statutory threshold, submit the environmental impact assessment tier determination and obtain a fire safety certificate from the local fire station. If the company physically supplies vessels, also register as a marine fuel oil supplier with the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and enter into a bank-operated standby letter of credit facility for settlement. The company must maintain a safety management plan, spill response plan, and qualified person-in-charge under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.
required_dossiers: Petroleum wholesale business registration application
Certified copy of the court corporate registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and business registration certificate
Title or lease of storage tanks and terminal facilities if applicable
Fire safety commencement certificate and civil defense inspection report
EIA decision letter or small-scale EIA approval
Foreign investment certificate and tax registration certificate
Port and marine fuel operation agreement if bunkering
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the petroleum license is challenged or suspended, file a written objection with the local government or MOTIE within 30 days and submit a corrected safety management plan. If environmental review flags non-compliance, supplement the impact assessment data to the Ministry of Environment and KECO and complete corrective measures before license activation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy of the Republic of Korea, Petroleum and Gas Division, together with the delegated local Si/Gun/Gu government licensing window and the Korea Petroleum Supply Association for technical review; the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries must also approve marine fuel supply activity if bunkering is performed.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Petroleum Wholesale Business Registration under the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act, and Marine Fuel Oil Supplier Registration under the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries where the company physically supplies vessels; additionally, a Dangerous Substances Storage or Handling Permit under the Chemical Substances Control Act is required when owning or occupying fuel tanks.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea with technical review by the Korea Environment Corporation (KECO).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 1 Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required when refined petroleum product storage or handling capacity is equal to or above 20,000 kl, or when the facility footprint equals or exceeds 1,000 square meters. Category 2 Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment applies to storage capacity from 2,000 kl up to 20,000 kl. Category 3 Environmental Registration is sufficient for capacity below 2,000 kl with secondary containment, oil-water separators, and a spill response plan. If the company acts solely as a paper broker with neither fuel storage nor physical handling, the facility-related EIA tier is Not Applicable, but the petroleum wholesale license and fire safety registration remain mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: VOC emissions from loading arms, tank vents, and pump seals must not exceed 100 mg/m3 at the outlet of any installed abatement equipment; facilities emitting 10 tonnes or more of VOCs per year must file a VOC emission report and install recovery or incineration systems. Wastewater discharged from tank dewatering, oil-water separators, or truck washing must comply with Korean industrial effluent thresholds of BOD 30 mg/L, COD 40 mg/L, SS 30 mg/L, total nitrogen 60 mg/L, total phosphorus 4 mg/L, and total petroleum hydrocarbons 5 mg/L. Hazardous sludge, filter media, and absorbent waste must be stored with secondary containment for no more than six months and manifested through the Korean electronic waste-tracking system to an authorized treatment facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Fighting Facilities Certificate and Civil Defense Safety Inspection from the local fire station under the National Fire Agency; structural load inspection certificate for tank foundations and pipe racks from a licensed structural engineer; workplace safety and health risk assessment approval under the Occupational Safety and Health Act filed with the regional office of the Ministry of Employment and Labor; chemical release and emergency response plan approved for any dangerous substance storage; and certification of fire extinguishing equipment adequacy before the storage or distribution facility may begin operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr); export and foreign-trade records are integrated through the Korea Customs Service (KCS) UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Appoint a domestic tax representative (certified tax accountant or licensed tax attorney) for the non-resident equity holder and execute a power of attorney to act before the NTS. Step 2: Obtain the mandatory petroleum wholesale licence under the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act and any marine-fuel bunker supplier authorisation, because the NTS business registration file requires the statutory licence number. Step 3: Incorporate the Chusik Hoesa at the Korean court registry and open a Korean bank account to receive export settlements. Step 4: Submit the Business Registration application through HomeTax or directly to the competent district NTS tax office using the company's Korean principal place of business; attach certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, board resolution naming the domestic tax representative and registered office, lease or ownership evidence for the business premise, and foreign parent/investor corporate documents. Step 5: Upon verification, NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions simultaneously as the entity TIN and VAT registration number; a separate VAT ID is not issued. Step 6: Activate the corporate HomeTax electronic certificate, register for the NTS-certified e-invoice API/EDI channel, and obtain a UNI-PASS trader ID for export declarations. There is no minimum capital requirement for tax registration, and 100% foreign ownership does not change the procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None relevant to entity classification. A Chusik Hoesa is automatically taxed as a domestic resident corporation on worldwide income under the Corporate Tax Act; the Republic of Korea has no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. A group consolidation election under the Corporate Tax Act may be available but does not alter the entity-level tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold applies to a stock corporation: the Chusik Hoesa is required to register for VAT from the first taxable supply. The Korean small-business VAT exemption threshold (KRW 80 million for goods and KRW 30 million for services, as adjusted by statute) is available only to individual entrepreneurs, not to a corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All corporate VAT taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax repository or an NTS-certified EDI/API integration. The e-tax invoice is transmitted to the NTS at the time of issuance and receives an NTS reference number that is used for anti-fraud matching with customs and bank foreign-exchange data; paper tax invoices are not permitted for a corporate trader. For zero-rated export and cross-border supplies, the electronic invoice must carry the relevant export declaration reference and the 0% zero-rated output VAT amount. Although Korea does not use a pre-approval digital stamping system, the mandatory NTS e-invoice repository and UNI-PASS integration operate as a real-time fiscal clearance layer for export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 26 of the Value-Added Tax Act zero-rates goods exported from Korea when an export declaration is accepted by Korea Customs Service and the goods are physically moved out of Korea. For marine fuel oil, distillates and crude-oil products, zero-rating also applies to bunker supplies delivered to foreign-going vessels engaged in international voyages and to international aircraft, as well as to qualifying export brokerage/commission services supplied to a non-resident counterparty for the underlying physical export trade. The supplier must prove the goods left Korea, the vessel/aircraft was in international trade (for bunkers), and the foreign-currency settlement was received from abroad. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated sales is refundable through the NTS VAT return system.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: KCS UNI-PASS export declaration acceptance certificate (Export Declaration Certificate) covering the crude oil, distillates or marine fuel cargo
Commercial invoice, sale/purchase contract, packing list, and quantity/quality certificate for the cargo
Ocean or multimodal Bill of Lading, or KCS-accepted electronic export transport document
Bunker Delivery Note and vessel master's signed receipt confirming the vessel or aircraft is employed in international navigation (for bunker zero-rating)
Bank-issued foreign-exchange receipt certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing the inward remittance from the foreign buyer, equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Information System, with policy and supervisory coordination by the Ministry of Economy and Finance; BOK exercises indirect capital-flow management and surveillance rather than a black-market rationing regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea is not a hard surrender-based exchange-control state but a fully-notified managed float regime. Current-account transactions, notably export and import settlements, service payments, dividends, royalties and cross-border trade finance, are generally liberalized under FETA and require only report-based verification through a designated Foreign Exchange Bank. Capital-account transactions are formulated under the capital account liberalization schedule: inbound foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa is permitted after filing a foreign investment report with the Ministry of Economy and Finance/Bank of Korea through a local bank or KOTRA, and funds must be held in a designated foreign currency account until certificate of capital verification. There is no forced surrender of export foreign currency to BOK, but export proceeds must be either converted into KRW via a licensed FX bank or retained in a domestic foreign-currency deposit account before the statutory collection deadline. Profit remittance is administratively workable but not frictionless: dividends require audited financial statements or a certified balance sheet, corporate tax payment verification, board resolution with the corporate seal, and a beneficial-ownership attestation; the remitting bank will also screen for sanctions and verify the non-resident shareholder's ultimate identity. Foreign currency loans and trade financing over threshold volumes are reportable and must contain genuine economic substance. Overall, the KR regime is compliant for an energy commodity trading entity if in-country banking is used and all transactions are recorded with the correct purpose codes and BOK/FIU reporting protocols.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, the default statutory export settlement period is 18 months from the date the export declaration is accepted; an extension may be granted by the designated foreign exchange bank for legitimate delays such as trade disputes, deferred payment terms, or force majeure conditions. There is no fixed mandatory conversion/surrender ratio to KRW. The exporter must choose, within the settlement window, to convert the receipts into KRW through an authorized FX bank or deposit them in a domestic foreign-currency account opened with a licensed bank; every receipt and conversion must be logged to the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Information System with the related export declaration number and transaction purpose code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Currency FDI Account) and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD multi-currency)
Basic Operational Currency Account and Standby Letter of Credit Facility Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low: offshore digital EMI services are legally non-viable as the primary treasury or clearing bank for a South Korean resident legal entity. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, any cross-border settlement, export receipt, import disbursement, or FX conversion must be processed through a licensed Foreign Exchange Bank in Korea. Offshore EMIs do not hold a Korean banking license, cannot open a domestic foreign-currency account for a Chusik Hoesa, and cannot file the mandatory BOK/FIU reports. Use of an offshore EMI for corporate operating payments may trigger AML, tax and foreign-exchange-reporting violations. At best, a non-bank payment system may process small local collections, but it cannot handle crude oil/refined products trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch attendance is required in practice. A statutory director or a locally appointed director with a board-authorized power of attorney must appear before a corporate relationship manager and compliance officer; remote consular proxy opening alone, without a branch visit or local proxy, is not accepted under Korean Real-Name Financial Transactions Act and FATF-compliant KYC procedures. If the foreign director cannot visit Seoul, the bank will require a notarized and apostilled power of attorney to a Korean resident representative and a video interview of the foreign director, passport notarization, corporate seal certificate, and shareholders/UBO statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex offshore ownership architecture using non-public-registry intermediate entities, causing unresolved ultimate beneficial ownership and high-risk classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership chart with notarized passport copies of all underlying natural persons; certificate of incumbency or registry abstract from every intermediate jurisdiction; tax residence certificates; audited financial statements of the intermediate holding company; signed Korea FIU UBO declaration; bank reference letters from existing banking partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity trade-based money-laundering red flags: invoice or pricing deviations from recognized oil benchmarks, unusual split shipments, transshipment in ports of concern, and shell counterparties without operating substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master sale and purchase agreements, trade confirmations referencing Platts/Argus pricing curves; full vessel track including IMO number, cargo documents (bill of lading, certificate of origin, quality certificate, insurance), customs import/export declarations; electronic AIS/GNSS logs with no coverage gaps; proof of bunker supplier and end-user relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and maritime red flags, particularly vessel calls or counterparties connected with North Korea, Russia, Iran, Venezuela, or UN/OFAC/EU/Korea designated persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Live OFAC, EU, UN, and Korean FIU sanctions-screening reports for all counterparties, banks, vessels and vessel owners; vessel screening report from a commercial maritime risk database; charter-party and vessel-owner KYC pack; AIS/transponder history and port state inspection records; contractual sanctions and no-redistribution warranties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence or inadequacy of the statutory petroleum business license and insufficient source of wholesale trading capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of corporate registration; petroleum wholesale/brokering license and annual validity; capital verification certificate or bank-certified shareholder remittances; opening balance sheet and anticipated monthly trading volumes; board resolution authorizing account opening and transaction threshold; three-to-six months of pre-account trading contracts and supplier inventories.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholders' capital is remitted via an international SWIFT wire (MT103/MT202) in USD or KRW to the Chusik Hoesa's designated foreign-currency account held at a licensed Korean Foreign Exchange Bank. The remitter must reference the Foreign Investment Promotion Act report number in the payment narrative, and the beneficiary bank will apply the inbound funds to the BOK Foreign Exchange Information System with an inward foreign exchange purpose code corresponding to equity investment in a domestic corporation. Within the statutory period, the bank issues a foreign currency investment certificate (capital verification certificate) confirming the remitted amount, exchange rate, date, and bank reference, which is then used for registration and corporate capital increases at the court registry. Any KRW conversion must be booked through the same bank and carry the capital-verification FX contract number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For downstream refined-product and crude oil disbursements, the Chusik Hoesa will use SWIFT Oversea Remittance MT103 with back-to-back trade documentation, or an Standby Letter of Credit/Commercial Letter of Credit when the beneficiary requires bank undertaking. A documentary collection is acceptable only for tested, low-sanctions-risk counterparties and requires a signed purchase agreement, verified bill of lading, certificate of quality/quantity, and payment schedule. For KRW-denominated vendor payments inside Korea, clearing is achieved through BOK-Wire+ / domestic KFTC rails. The bank will verify each outward transfer against an underlying trade contract and, when necessary, the exporter's foreign exchange purchased/sold record, ensuring that payments do not exceed documented invoice values and that maritime disbursements are covered by a confirmation of cargo/vessel identity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/KRW FX forward booked with a licensed domestic Foreign Exchange Bank, subject to the Korean 'real demand' principle and supported by the underlying energy trade contract or receivables/payables schedule.

Cross-currency interest-rate or basis swap between USD and KRW used solely to hedge long-term external financing or capital-loan exposure, with prior BOK/FX bank reporting and no speculative net open position.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) can only be used where the trade-leg currency is a non-KRW exotic pair or where the bank approves a back-to-back NDF with a foreign counterparty; a Korean resident energy trader may not run an open NDF position against KRW outside the BOK real-demand framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the deadline is March 31 of the following year. A one-month extension is allowed for companies whose financial statements are separately audited by an external certified CPA auditor, making the extended deadline April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpaid corporate tax attracts an underreport penalty of 10% (up to 20% when the underreported amount is over 3 billion KRW or consistent tax evasion is found), a non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax amount, and heavy negligence penalties up to 40% of the wrongful underreport amount for unjustified omission. Annual interest accrues at 3.3% per month from the original due date. The NTS can compulsory collect arrears by seizing bank accounts, receivables, and other property. Persistent non-filing or non-payment may lead to the government initiating corporate dissolution but not an administrative strike-off; the entity's business registration can be forcibly closed after continued delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Metropolitan City or Province tax office where the company's registered head office is located)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the same date as the national corporate income tax return: March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end, with a one-month extension to April 30 if the extension applies to the national tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment by the statutory deadline triggers a 1.2% monthly late payment surcharge for the first 12 months, increasing to 1.5% per month thereafter. Failure to file the local corporate tax return carries an additional 20% penalty on the unpaid local tax amount. The locality may issue an administrative demand, and continued non-payment allows seizure of assets and liquidation of unpaid dues through compulsory means.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA), filed through the external audit management system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after the certified auditor issues the final audit report, and in all cases before the annual general shareholding meeting that approves the financial statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of the audit report is subject to an administrative fine of up to 20 million KRW per occurrence. If the statutory audit is omitted entirely, the FSS may impose a negligence penalty up to 50 million KRW on the company, and the responsible external auditor may be subject to prosecution or license restrictions. For listed enterprises and financial institutions, such noncompliance also triggers a marked corporate governance audit deficiency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Petroleum Enterprise Sales and Inventory Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea National Oil Corporation (KNOC) data reporting portal, with a copy to the Regional Oil Distribution Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than January 31 for the preceding calendar year. Monthly movements (receipts, storage, sales, exports, imports) must also be reported on a monthly basis by the 10th of the following month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual petroleum movement report or submission of false data is punishable by an administrative fine of up to 30 million KRW under the Petroleum and Petroleum Alternative Fuel Business Act. Habitual or willful noncompliance may lead to suspension of the petroleum wholesale license for up to 6 months and, in severe cases, license revocation, effectively terminating the enterprise's legal authorization to operate in the crude oil and refined products wholesale sector.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Compliance Report (for Non-Resident Shareholders)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) prescribed authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of the statutory general shareholders' meeting if the company has foreign investors, or upon request of the investment protection agency. Additionally, any capital movement, share transfer, or modification of the foreign investment registry must be reported to the relevant foreign exchange bank within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to a fine of 5 million KRW; knowingly filing false information is punishable by imprisonment or a penalty up to 10 million KRW. If the errant company is a foreign-invested entity, the non-compliance may also affect the foreign investor's eligibility for tax deductions, tariff exemption, and the acquisition of additional foreign exchange permissions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (as amended), an independent CPA audit is mandatory for any company that: (1) has total assets of 12 billion KRW or more at the end of the fiscal year; (2) is listed or publicly offered; (3) has not been exempted despite total assets lower than 12 billion KRW because it satisfies certain combined tests under the FSC Enforcement Decree, including cases where annual revenue exceeds 100 billion KRW or the company records average headcount of more than 300 employees; (4) is a financial institution, investment banker, mutual savings bank, or securities term such that it is specified in the FSS's asset and revenue tests; or (5) is otherwise designated by the Financial Supervisory Commission to be within the statutory external audit scope for the protection of investors and public interest. In addition, a company that is not individually subject to external audit must still appoint an external auditor if a consolidated parent entity having control over it meets the mandatory audit requirement (consolidated threshold of total assets 120 billion KRW).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Mandatory audited companies must apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board. Non-public companies below the external audit threshold but voluntarily preparing audited or unaudited statutory financial statements may apply the Korea SME Accounting Standards (K-GAAP for Non-Public Entities) which is aligned with the basic requirements of K-IFRS. For all companies, the financial statements must be prepared in accordance with the Commercial Act and the external audit law, and they must show true and fair value in compliance with K-IFRS where applicable. A certified public accountant registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants must sign the audit opinion.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate a single central public beneficial ownership registry comparable to the EU-style UBO regime. Instead, under the Commercial Act and the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Secret, every Chusik Hoesa must maintain and annually review its Register of Members (shareholder registry) and must keep the register open for inspection by shareholders, creditors, and the tax authorities. Any transfer of shares, pledge registration, or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the shareholder registry promptly at the time of transfer. For non-listed companies, the transfer becomes effective with the intent of both parties, but the company is only bound to treat the transferee as a shareholder upon endorsement of the share certificate and update of the shareholder registry. There is no statutory 30-day filing to a government corporate registry in the ordinary case; however, the tax authorities require that any transfer of shares of a non-listed company must be reported for stock transfer tax (local tax) within 30 days from the transfer date at the district tax office. If a share transfer occurs with a change in the largest shareholder exceeding 30% of the issued shares, the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act rules on foreign direct investment disclosures may oblige a 30-day report to the receiving bank or to the National Tax Service regarding the ultimate beneficial owner. The company's external auditor will review the accuracy of the shareholder registry as part of the annual statutory audit, and inaccurate registers may lead to audit qualifications and a penalty of up to 10 million KRW on the company under the External Audit Enforcement Rules. The beneficial owner of any corporate account must be identified under the real-name financial transaction system, and a bank or financial institution may request an annual beneficial ownership statement from the company as part of its anti-money-laundering due diligence. This statement must be confirmed by the registered director or statutory representative, and failure to provide accurate information constitutes a criminal offense carrying imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine up to 30 million KRW.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: National Corporate Income Tax at progressive marginal rates: 10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 20% on taxable income from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 22% on taxable income from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; and 24% on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion. A local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of the national corporate tax is superimposed, yielding effective combined marginal rates of 11%, 22%, 24.2%, and 26.4% respectively. For wholesale energy trading profits above KRW 300 billion, the effective top rate is 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No industry-specific statutory tax holiday is available for wholesale trading of crude oil or refined petroleum products in South Korea. Available preferential regimes include: (i) foreign investment tax exemptions or 50% reductions for five to seven years in designated Foreign Investment Zones under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; (ii) credits under the Tax Incentive and Limitation Control Act, including research and development expenditure credits of up to 30% of eligible R&D spend, employment promotion credits, and facility investment credits ranging from 4% to 6% of eligible investment; (iii) the foreign tax credit mechanism under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, which credits foreign income taxes against Korean corporate tax on foreign-source income subject to a per-country limitation; and (iv) the net operating loss carryforward regime allowing a 10-year carryforward, with the annual deduction capped at 80% of current-year taxable income for SMEs and 60% for non-SMEs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Interim Prepayment Corporate Tax Return and Tax Base Computed Schedule filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal at www.hometax.go.kr or, for taxpayers designated as large corporations, through approved electronic tax filing software such as i-PRO.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within two months after the close of the first six months of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year company the interim prepayment is due by 31 August.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: legal name, 10-digit corporate business registration number, representative director name, jurisdictional tax office, and business classification codes for wholesale trade.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation owned by non-residents must file using its Korean business registration number and disclose the foreign shareholders addresses in the shareholder schedule; the filing itself is made by the Korean entity and not by the foreign shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interim taxable base: calculate the preliminary taxable income under the prior-year-basis method, generally 50% of the immediately preceding year national tax adjusted for current-year circumstances, or elect the actual first-half profit method where permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders should ensure the elected method incorporates transfer pricing adjustments so that related-party transactions with the Korean entity are reflected at arm's length values.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interim prepayment tax: compute national corporate tax at the 10% to 24% progressive rates, add the 10% local income tax surcharge, and deduct prior withholding credits and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any Korean withholding tax on dividends or interest paid to the foreign shareholder during the interim period may be offset in this box only if supported by official withholding tax certificates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or late filing of the interim prepayment return attracts a non-filing addition of 20% of the unpaid interim tax, reduced to 10% for SMEs, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022% of the unpaid amount from the day after the statutory deadline to the settlement date. The National Tax Service may also seize assets to enforce collection without a separate formal assessment.
